name: Eduardo Avaroa Andean Fauna National Reserve
blurb: Pink salt lagoons, three flamingos and the vicuñas, foxes and pumas of the puna.

tip.title: Bleach the lagoon
tip.text: The pink algae feed brine shrimp and all three flamingos. Set Pink lagoon algae to -80% and watch the flamingos, then the culpeo and puma that hunt on the plains.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Eduardo Avaroa Andean Fauna National Reserve

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Puna bunchgrasses
nodes.desc: Clump-forming grasses such as Festuca and Stipa dominate the puna grasslands. They are the main food of the camelids on the plains.

nodes.name: Diatoms
nodes.desc: Microscopic glass-walled algae that live on the lake bottom and in the water. Andean and James's flamingos feed mainly on them.
A rock-dwelling rodent that eats mostly grasses and moss and stays close to rocky shelter. The most recorded wild rodent here.
Small crustaceans of salty lakes that filter algae from the water. A flamingo and avocet food source; the exact species here is not confirmed.
Filters algae, plankton, crustaceans and other small invertebrates from shallow lakes and lagoons.

nodes.name: Culpeo (Andean fox)
nodes.desc: An opportunistic fox that eats rodents, hares, birds and carrion, and sometimes young camelids and flamingos. Livestock owners often blame it.
A huge scavenger that lives in the puna and feeds on carcasses. The Wikipedia puna page lists it among the ecoregion birds.
The top predator of the puna. Hunts vicuñas and other camelids and also takes viscachas, and may kill culpeos.

nodes.name: Soil microbes
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, dung and carcasses slowly in the cold, dry air, returning nutrients to the soil.
